Lossless re-encode. Keep the format as PNG and Squish rewrites the file through the browser's encoder, dropping EXIF, color profiles and text chunks. Savings are modest on already-optimized files, which is why the Keep smaller option returns the original when nothing was gained.

Lossless compression (PNG, WebP lossless) rearranges data more efficiently without changing a single pixel. Savings are modest, usually 5–30%, and come mostly from stripping metadata and better encoding. Lossy compression (JPEG, WebP lossy) approximates the image and can shrink files by 70–90%. For photos, lossy at quality 75–85 is almost always the right call; for graphics with sharp edges and flat colors, stick with lossless PNG.

Shared hosting commonly caps uploads at 2–8 MB per file via upload_max_filesize. A pre-compressed image never gets near that. Squish's output also drops EXIF and GPS tags, which WordPress would otherwise store, and names files name-min.jpg so originals and optimized versions never collide.

Squish compresses, resizes and converts images entirely inside your web browser using the HTML5 Canvas API. When you add an image, it is read into your browser's memory, processed there, and offered back to you as a download. No image, filename or metadata is ever transmitted to our servers or to any third party. We have no server-side component that could receive your files. Once you close or reload the page, the images are gone from memory.
